doc.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995

title: Learning Basie's cues and the rhythm section with John Clayton
summary: Reading Basie's gestures, joining in August 1979, and John Clayton on bass.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: only to their opinion. But the main thing is that I kept my eyes on the Count at all times and he gave me all the cues, you know, whether it was a wink of the eye or a little pinky here, or just a shrug of the shoulder, or anything, I knew what he wanted. And he taught me so much. He didn’t even have to say anything, he just had to look at me you know. And I feel in my own heart that the dear Lord above put me on this earth to be the Count Basie drummer. And I was so blessed to have that opportunity to play with the Count.
Yeah. It’s an awesome responsibility to be in that rhythm section. Who was playing bass at that time?

Well at that particular time the first three months, I joined August 12 of 1979. And I stayed at that point a full year. And the bassist for the first three months I was there was John Clayton, who is an extraordinary player, he really is, he’s great, whether in symphonic work or straight ahead jazz. And he’s become one of the most prolific arrangers and composers and I love his writing. And he stayed for three months, but he had been on the band a few years and he wanted to settle down with his family in Los Angeles and start to work in the studios. You know he’s been extremely successful with that. And then a gentleman came on the band, Cleveland Eaton. He had played with Ramsey Lewis and a few people.
